core_obligations: (a) is equivalent to (b) (proof lines 7505-7507): the left adjoint v is right exact, and combined with the characterization of exactness of functors this explains the equivalence.

(a) implies (c) (proof lines 7509-7520): for an injective object I, a monomorphism phi : N -> M in the target category and a morphism alpha : N -> uI, adjointness produces a morphism vN -> I and the assumption makes v(phi) injective; injectivity of I extends to vM -> I, and adjointness turns the extension back, so uI is injective.

(c) implies (a) assuming enough injectives (proof lines 7522-7528): for a monomorphism f : B -> B' with A = ker(v(f)), one chooses a monomorphism g : A -> I into an injective object, extends it first to v(B) and then by adjunction and injectivity of u(I) to a morphism B' -> u(I), which adjoints back to a morphism v(B') -> I extending the earlier one; since g was a monomorphism this forces A = 0, so v(f) is injective.
proof_roadmap: Identify the equivalence of injectivity-preservation and exactness of the left adjoint.
Use the extension property of an injective object and adjointness to prove injectivity of the image.
Use enough injectives and the extension property in the target to recover injectivity-preservation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates three conditions on an adjoint pair of additive functors between abelian categories, namely that the left adjoint preserves monomorphisms, that it is exact, and that the right adjoint preserves injectives, and shows that the first two are equivalent and imply the third, with all three equivalent when the source has enough injectives (statement lines 7486-7502). The proof is a complete argument: the first equivalence is reduced to right exactness of a left adjoint together with the characterization of exactness (proof lines 7505-7507); the implication to preservation of injectives is a two-step adjointness computation with the extension property (proof lines 7509-7520); and the converse uses enough injectives and the extension property in the target category (proof lines 7522-7528). The non-formal content is the adjointness bookkeeping in the two implications. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
